status: Final practical research recommendation for the measured distribution
general_rules: Read the relevant code before changing it.
Write the simplest code that solves the task: no features, abstractions or options nobody asked for.
Change only what the task needs, and match the surrounding code's style. Mention unrelated problems you notice instead of fixing them; remove only what your own change left unused.
After changing code, run the project's build or tests and read the result. If you couldn't, say so.

Ask before destructive or outward-facing actions (deleting files, git push, anything outside the project). If a request can be read several ways, name the readings and ask instead of picking one silently.
Finish with 2–4 sentences: what changed, how you checked it, what's left. Name files by path.
decision: Retain the existing baseline. Compact tied ordinary operational success, had fewer saved-code passes and no confirmed token saving; context shows a tradeoff rather than uniform dominance. The predeclared protocol permits baseline fallback when replacement is unjustified. This does not establish universal optimality or statistically proven baseline superiority.
limits: Finite authored tasks, mutable model aliases, exploratory intervals and incomplete usage prevent a universal-best, causal quality or actual monetary-cost claim. All original frozen assets and raw grades remain unchanged.
